history.summary: A small, refined mid-13th-century Hoysala temple dedicated to Vishnu as Chennakeshava, built in the ekakuta (single-shrine) plan with a 16-star pointed (stellate) vimana on a raised jagati. The sanctum holds a well-preserved Keshava image; the outer walls carry about 90 detailed sculptures of Vishnu's forms (some sources note unusual iconography, e.g. six-armed Vishnu figures). Protected monument under the Karnataka state division of the ASI. Patronage conflict: Wikipedia (citing Foekema) dates it to c. 1250 under King Vira Someshwara, while cultureandheritage.org attributes it to Veera Ballala II — flag for verify. Town correction: the temple is at Aralaguppe village in Tiptur taluk (known as 'Alariguppe' in inscriptions), not Tumkur town. Festivals listed are typical observances (verify locally); one travel source claims it was built as a Hoysala 'demo temple' (unverified).

name: Sri Chennakeshava Temple, Aralaguppe
town_description: Aralaguppe is a small village in Tiptur taluk of Tumakuru district, about 65 km from Tumakuru. It is known for this 13th-century Hoysala Chennakeshava temple and lies 6 km from Banasandra railway station.

travel.railway: Banasandra railway station (~6 km); Tumakuru station (~65 km)
travel.road: ~65 km from Tumakuru; muddy village road off the main road — a private vehicle is advisable

visitor_information.opening_hours: ASI-protected shrine; typical hours ~6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 5:00-8:00 PM (verify locally)
